supersedes_prose_in: data/foreign_voice/lexicon.json reading_rules ('PRECEDENCE IS CARRIED, NOT REBUILT')
purpose: The canonical grouping rule of DESIGN-voice-completion 3.1, frozen and
digested BEFORE the renderer changes, and carrying the same status rule R
and the lexicon carry: a TRUSTED, REVIEWED ARTIFACT, not renderer logic.
It exists because v0.19 voided on C-V4.drop_group at 0.80 against a 0.90
floor, for one mechanical reason: deleting a semantically redundant
bracket changes the sentence and not the term. A served sentence could
therefore have a variant that reads differently and certifies identically,
and a reader could not tell which one the graph meant.
The repair is structural. After this rule a redundant grouping variant is
not rare, it is UNGRAMMATICAL -- and G1b says so over every surviving pair
why_an_artifact_and_not_code: The rule is a claim about a parser this repository did not write. If it is
wrong, the inverse hands the pinned binary a term that re-associates and B1
fails loudly, everywhere -- the good failure mode.
A digested file makes widening it a diff with a review, which is rule R's
3.2 discipline, and it is what the per-statement pair classification is
how_the_levels_were_obtained: MEASURED against the pinned toolchain (leanprover/lean4:v4.32.2) on
2026-08-24, before this file was written and before any renderer changed.
For each ordered pair of operators the probe elaborated `a OP1 b OP2 c`
and its two bracketings and compared the serialized Expr digests through
scripts/foreign_voice_oracle.py; the bracketing whose digest matched the
flat form is the one the toolchain builds.
Associativity was read the same way from `a OP b OP c`, and the
non-associative operators were confirmed by the flat form FAILING to
elaborate -- `a = b = c` and `P ↔ Q ↔ R` are not terms in this toolchain.
This table is therefore what the binary does, not what a manual says. G1
re-checks all of it over 2,313 covered statements, because one wrong level
is wrong everywhere and a single disagreement stops the cycle.

levels.note: loosest. Chaining rejected by the toolchain: `P ↔ Q ↔ R` fails.
the ASCII spelling the residue also carries; same relation, same level
55 covered statements spell it this way; the v0.19 lexicon gained a row for it by dated correction

prefix.measured: `¬ a = b` elaborates as `¬ (a = b)` and `¬ P ∧ Q` as `(¬ P) ∧ Q`, so ¬ binds looser than a relation and tighter than a connective
`-a * b` elaborates as `(-a) * b` and `-a ^ 2` as `-(a ^ 2)`, so unary minus binds tighter than `*` and looser than `^`

binder_tail_rule.statement: a binder body extends maximally right, so a binder needs brackets IFF it is not in tail position
tail_propagates_through: the right operand of an infix operator, when that operator is itself in tail position
the argument of a prefix operator, when the prefix is itself in tail position
the body of a binder (always tail within the binder's extent)
the inside of any bracket pair, which re-establishes tail position
tail_is_lost_at: the left operand of any infix operator, and nothing else

a_bracket_restores_tail.statement: inside a bracket the extent ends at the matching `)`, so whatever sits rightmost inside it IS in tail position there
why_it_is_called_out: The first transcription of this clause said the opposite -- that a node
which had to be bracketed loses tail position inside its own bracket --
and the two halves of the rule then contradicted each other.
It cost exactly ONE statement in 2,313: lean_workbook_plus_82031's
`(B → ∀ x y z : Rat, body)` was re-emitted as
`(B → (∀ x y z : Rat, body))`, a bracket the source did not write.
The census's `it_can_only_remove` check is what caught it, which is the
whole reason that check exists: a rule that can add a bracket is not a
canonicalization, and one counterexample refutes the claim as

measured: `∀ x : Rat, x = x ∧ x = x` elaborates identically to `∀ x : Rat, (x = x ∧ x = x)` -- the body swallows the conjunction.
`¬ ∃ x : Rat, x = x` elaborates identically to `¬ (∃ x : Rat, x = x)`, so a binder under a prefix in tail position needs no bracket and `¬ ∃ x : Rat, p` is ALREADY canonical.
`(∀ x : Rat, x = x) ∧ z = z` needs its bracket: the left operand of `∧` is not tail position.
why_it_is_a_clause_and_not_an_emergent_p: Correction 3: this is a rule someone had to supply. It is not derivable
from a precedence table, because a binder has no precedence -- it is
bracketed by POSITION. A reader reproducing this design must not have to

binder_group_rule.statement: a parenthesised binder group `∃ (x y z : Rat),` is re-emitted WITHOUT its brackets as `∃ x y z : Rat,`
binder_group_rule.measured: `∃ (x y : Rat), x = y` and `∃ x y : Rat, x = y` elaborate to byte-identical serializations
binder_group_rule.scope: 16 covered statements carry a binder-group bracket, 16 brackets in all; one of them, lean_workbook_54220, is in the sealed hundred
why_it_is_a_clause: Correction 3: this is a real change to 16 surfaces that NO precedence
argument produces. The bracketed form is the one the corpus wrote, and
both forms mean the same thing, so the rule has to choose -- and a rule
that chooses has to say so out loud rather than leave the choice inside

ascription_rule.statement: `(e : T)` is SYNTAX. Its brackets are the ascription; they are never a grouping pair, never counted in a grouping census, never mutated, and never removed
ascription_rule.scope: 149 covered statements carry at least one ascription, 215 ascription brackets in all; after canonicalization 42 statements' only remaining bracket pair is an ascription
why_it_matters_beyond_correctness: All three kinds render through the SAME two lexicon rows -- `the
quantity` and `end quantity` -- so a mutation pool that admits on the
phrase appearing in a surface cannot tell them apart. v0.19's drop_group
pool did exactly that: G5b measures 1,518 of its 1,549 admitting through
a real grouping pair, so 31 were padding the denominator of a control
about grouping with statements that had no grouping bracket at all.

emit_rule.statement: bracket a child IFF the child's level is below the position's minimum for that operand side
emit_rule.atoms: an identifier or numeral binds tighter than every operator and is never bracketed
emit_rule.binders: bracketed by POSITION under binder_tail_rule, never by level

it_can_only_remove.claim: this rule never ADDS a bracket the source omitted
it_can_only_remove.argument: a source statement parses, so the structure it denotes already follows precedence, and the canonical form of a parsing source can only remove
it_can_only_remove.checked_not_assumed: experiments/grouping_census.json publishes the per-statement delta distribution; there is no negative bucket across 2,313 statements

used_by: G1b, whose 5,228-pair census is over grouping pairs only
G5b, whose floor is zero cross-kind mutation records in drop_group and shift_group

not_claimed: No readability claim. The rule says how much surface changes, not whether
the change helps a reader. DESIGN-voice-completion 8 keeps that open with
a live example: lean_workbook_20627 canonicalizes to four disjuncts with
no grouping word anywhere, and only C-V3 could say whether that helped.
No claim that the levels are Lean's documented levels. They are the levels
the PINNED BINARY was measured to use, which is the only thing the inverse
